A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CyberGym, with matching benchmark foundations and central experiments. The main texts and Appendices A–F, including tables, figures, and agent traces, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of eleven LLMs and four agent frameworks, behavioral analyses, and vulnerability discoveries.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical evaluations and adds an expert audit, statistical comparisons, balanced scoring, and quantitative failure analyses.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction and filtering procedure, PoC-generation workflow, and four information levels are retained. The added validation analyses and implementation disclosures do not establish a new proposed algorithm or model.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the 1,507-instance benchmark across 188 projects, four information levels, and open-ended discovery across 431 projects and 1,748 executables. The new audits and subgroup analyses examine existing source and benchmark coverage; the ARVO/recent-instance breakdown is additional documentation.

E2.justification: The contamination comparison expands from Claude-3.7-Sonnet and GPT-4.1 to include GPT-5 with minimal reasoning and o4-mini (v3 Table 2). The main eleven-model and four-agent comparison sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds a stratified 300-sample expert-audit protocol and project/crash-type-balanced scoring, and specifies a greater-than-50 post-cutoff sample criterion for contamination analysis. Section 5 also reports updating incompletely patched reference versions to fully fixed versions. These substantially extend validation procedures and revise evaluation targets, without establishing that the retained headline experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds validation of filtering/rephrasing, checks PoC-length distributions across cutoff cohorts, tests sensitivity to project and crash-type weighting, and reports crash-type and quantitative failure breakdowns. Three new failure traces supplement the retained command-use, PoC-length, execution-step, and earlier case-study analyses.

E5.justification: v3 introduces Fisher’s exact and two-proportion Z-tests for contamination comparisons, Cohen’s kappa of 0.82 ± 0.03 for annotation agreement, and ± reporting for retrieval counts in Table 9. v2 lacks comparable statistical reporting. Neither version specifies repeated-run or seed counts, and v3 does not define its ± quantities.

E6.justification: v3 adds 96% audit precision, 27.2% success for the union across models, balanced scores, and crash/failure breakdowns. Claude-3.7-Sonnet’s reported post-cutoff rate changes from 12.1% to 12.5%. Section 5 revises total zero-days from 35 to 34 and incomplete patches from 17 to 18, with one now affecting a latest version; CVE assignments increase from 3 to 4 and patched vulnerabilities from 6 to 10. Main performance-plot scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The task definitions and pre-/post-patch success criterion remain unchanged. Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs; the added statistical tests and empirical averaging procedures do not introduce new mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract’s discovery claim changes from 35 zero-days and 17 incomplete patches to 34 and 18. The benchmark-scale, difficulty, and practical-impact claims remain. However, v3’s introduction still retains the old breakdown of 17 incomplete patches and 10 reproduction-derived zero-days.

C2.justification: v3 adds real-world rationale for the information levels and concrete obstacles to future patching/exploitation evaluation. It replaces the speculative safety-alignment explanation for o4-mini with discussion of model-specific termination behavior and adds implications of the new failure analyses. The existing C/C++ and memory-safety scope limitation is retained.

D1.justification: v3 documents the 1,368 ARVO versus 139 newer instances, an approximately $3,000 full-evaluation cost, and provision of the existing 300-instance subset. Appendix C extends documented thinking-token budgets and tool-use exceptions to Claude-Sonnet-4. Hardware, model checkpoints, agent commits, and code/data access references remain unchanged; these disclosures do not establish reruns.

R1.justification: v3 adds references motivating memory-safety evaluation and one-day patch analysis, plus an introduction footnote citing CyberGym adoption in Claude, Kimi, and GLM evaluations. Section 2’s comparison with cybersecurity and coding benchmarks remains substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 expands explanations in Sections 3–4 and Appendices C–D, merges and reorders the vulnerability-discovery discussion in Section 5, and adds conference-header, affiliation, and acknowledgement edits. The overall section hierarchy and most existing prose and case studies are retained.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands visual evidence with audit/cohort distribution plots, balanced-comparison plots, contamination and diagnostic tables, and three failure-trace figures. Existing displays are retained across relocation and renumbering, with explicit Level 1 labels added to several performance plots.

improvement.justification: The expert audit and sensitivity/statistical analyses in Appendices C–D strengthen support for benchmark reliability. Section 5’s reported correction of incompletely patched reference versions also addresses an evaluation weakness. These benefits yield a limited net improvement: v3 leaves inconsistent vulnerability counts, undefined uncertainty quantities, and unclear linkage between corrected reference versions and unchanged headline scores.
